NETBANNER_FIRST: You are connected to the device's own network. Choose your Wi-Fi in Menu › Network.
NETBANNER_WEAK: Weak Wi-Fi signal ({DBM} dBm): commands may get lost
NETBANNER_FALLBACK: Ethernet cable unplugged: the device switched to Wi-Fi

LOGIN_SCOPE_ALL: The whole device asks you to sign in.
WELCOME_LEAD: Easily control and track your roller shutters, blinds, gates, garage doors or any other device using the RTS protocol.
WELCOME_NET_DESC: To get started, connect ESPSomfy-RTS to your internet box over Wi-Fi or Ethernet.
WELCOME_NET_DONE_WIFI: Done: the device has joined the Wi-Fi network
WELCOME_NET_DONE_ETH: Done: the device is connected to your network over Ethernet.
WELCOME_PREF_DESC: Time and location for your schedules, theme and color to your liking.
WELCOME_PREF_WAIT: Available once the device is connected to the internet, where it gets the time from.
WELCOME_RAD_DESC: Choose your radio module and turn it on, so the device can talk to your motors and hear your remotes.
WELCOME_RAD_DONE: The radio is on: the device can talk to your motors and hear your remotes.
WELCOME_ADD_DEVICE_DESC: Grab a remote, and your shutter, blind or gate answers from this screen.
WELCOME_FOOTER_NOTE: *Once a room, device, or group has been created, this page will no longer be displayed.
FIRST_CONNECT_WELCOME_DESC: {N} steps to connect the device to your network. It takes about two minutes.
FIRST_CONNECT_AP_NOTE: You are connected directly to the device, through its own Wi-Fi network (address 192.168.4.1). Once the wizard is finished, switch back to your usual network.
FIRST_CONNECT_MODE_TITLE: How does the device join your network?
FIRST_CONNECT_MODE_DESC: This choice determines the settings of the next step. You can change it later in Network › Connection.
FIRST_CONNECT_MODE_ETH_DESC: Wired or PoE connection, with no wireless fallback.
FIRST_CONNECT_MODE_BOTH_DESC: Cable first, Wi-Fi if the cable stops responding.
FIRST_CONNECT_NET_TITLE_WIFI: Connect the device to your Wi-Fi
FIRST_CONNECT_NET_TITLE_BOTH: The Ethernet board, then the backup Wi-Fi
FIRST_CONNECT_NET_LEAD_WIFI: The device has looked for nearby networks. Yours is probably the first one.
FIRST_CONNECT_ETH_SECTION_DESC: Select the Ethernet board your device uses to connect to the network.
FIRST_CONNECT_NET_LEAD_BOTH: Choose the Ethernet board, then the Wi-Fi that takes over if the cable stops responding.
FIRST_CONNECT_ETH_BOX_DESC: Ethernet requires no setup: your internet router will automatically assign an address to your device upon saving. Please configure the Wi-Fi below, which will take over in case of an Ethernet connection failure.
FIRST_CONNECT_ETH_AUTO: Your router will automatically assign an address to the device as soon as the cable is plugged in.
FIRST_CONNECT_PASS_HINT: Your router’s, often printed underneath it.
FIRST_CONNECT_HOSTNAME_DESC: This name makes it easy to find your device on the network (e.g. http://name.local).
FIRST_CONNECT_HINT_WIFI: Choose a network and enter its password
FIRST_CONNECT_HINT_FALLBACK: Choose the backup Wi-Fi and enter its password
FIRST_CONNECT_HINT_PASS: A Wi-Fi password has at least 8 characters
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_OK: The device is connecting to your network. Its own Wi-Fi network, named after the device, will disappear: this is normal.
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_BACK_D: Reconnect this phone or computer to your usual network.
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_OPEN_T: Open the interface at this address
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_OPEN_D: In your browser, once this phone or computer is back on your network.
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_IP_T: Address not responding? Go through your router
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_IP_D: Open your router’s interface (its address is often printed underneath), look for “{host}” in the list of connected devices, then type the IP address it was given into your browser, for example http://192.168.1.25.
FIRST_CONNECT_DONE_NEXT: Next: turn on the radio, then add your first device. The home page will guide you.

DASH_HOUSE_SUB: {n} device(s) · excluding gates, garage doors and awnings
DASH_EDIT_HINT: The eye hides or shows a card again. Order and rooms are set on the Devices, Groups and Rooms pages.
NO_DEVICE: No devices are currently assigned to this room. You can add or move devices in the settings menu.
DASHB_PREFS_MODAL_DESC: What the cards and the header show. Applies to every browser.
DASHB_PREFS_MOVEMENT_INDICATOR_DESC: Highlights the card that is moving.
DASHB_PREFS_REVERSE_COLUMNS_DESC: On a computer, swaps the Groups and Devices columns.
DASHB_PREFS_RADIO_ACTIVITY_DESC: A header icon moves with every signal.
CARD_MY_LIVE_HINT: Bring the device to the position you want, then save it.
CARD_MY_VALUE_HINT: Set the position that "my" should recall. The grey mark on the slider shows where the device is now.
CARD_OPT_CONFIRM_DESC: Useful for a garage door or a gate
CARD_OPT_HIDE_DESC: Still controlled by schedules and Home Assistant
CARD_PREFS_LOCAL_HINT: These display settings stay in this browser; nothing is written to the device.
VR_HOLD_HINT: Holding a key repeats the frame, as on the real remote. Prog only sends after being held for one second.
VR_COMBOS_NOTE: These combinations are used by setup procedures (direction of rotation, end limits, reset): one press too many can upset the motor’s settings.
VR_SENSOR_DESC: Simulates a frame from the sun and wind sensor.
VR_STEP_DESC: 80-bit frames. One press = one step of the chosen size.
PAGE_DEVICES_DESC: The shades, awnings and doors this device controls. Open a tile to set up a device.
LIST_ADD_DEVICE_DESC: The wizard guides you step by step
EMPTY_DEVICE_DESC: Add your first device: the wizard pairs it, then you control it from the dashboard.
DEVICE_CREATE_DESC: Save basic parameters to create your device
DEVICE_STATE_VOCAB_DESC: Terms used to report the status
DEVICE_LED_FEEDBACK_DESC: Flashes the status LED every time a command is sent to this device.
DEVICE_DELETE_DESC: A device that belongs to a group must be removed from it first. Its schedules are deleted with it.
DEVICE_TIMES_DESC: Measured by the wizard; correct them here if the displayed position drifts at the end of travel.
DEVICE_REMOTES_TIP: A linked remote keeps controlling the device; ESPSomfy-RTS listens to it to keep the displayed state up to date.
DEVICE_REPEAT_TIP: Motor hears a remote poorly? ESPSomfy-RTS can repeat it. {N}/{MAX} slots used.
DEVICE_REMOTE_REPEAT_OFF: If the motor hears it poorly
DEVICE_REMOTE_ADD_DESC: Then press one of its buttons
SETUP_W_COPY_DESC: Type, protocol, direction, travel times and options are copied; name, room, ID, remotes and My position are not. The copy is created right away.
SETUP_W_REMOTE_H: Do you already have a remote for it?
SETUP_W_REMOTE_NONE_DESC: Fine: the default settings suit most Somfy RTS motors. You will still need an already paired remote to open the motor’s memory when pairing.
SETUP_W_HINT_LISTEN: Press a button on the remote
SETUP_W_NAME_AUTO: Suggested from the type: change it freely. It is the name shown on the dashboard and in Home Assistant.
SETUP_W_CREATE_NOTE: “Create the device” saves it right away: it appears in the list and commissioning starts right here. You can stop at any time.
SETUP_W_PAIR_H: Let’s introduce the device to the motor
SETUP_W_CREATED: “{name}” has been created. Each next step is saved as you go.
SETUP_W_PAIR_LEAD: The motor only obeys remotes it knows: open its memory with an already paired remote, then the device introduces itself.
SETUP_W_HINT_PAIR: Open the memory, then press PROG
SETUP_W_DIR_TIP: If the device goes the wrong way, no need to pair it again: “The opposite” fixes the direction, and it can be changed at any time from its page.
SETUP_W_HINT_DIR: Test, then say what it did
SETUP_COPY_CONFIRM_DESC: Type, protocol, direction, travel times and options are copied. Name, room, ID, remotes and My position are not: pairing and My still need to be done.
SETUP_Q_BUTTONS: How many buttons on its remote?
SETUP_SW_STATE_DESC: Its state will show as “{on}” or “{off}”.
SETUP_CONTACT_LATCH_DESC: The contact stays closed until the next command (latching).
SETUP_CONTACT_PULSE_DESC: The contact closes briefly then opens again, like a push button.
SETUP_REMOTE_DESC: Press one of its buttons: the box recognises the protocol on its own, and the remote keeps working.
SETUP_LISTEN_DESC: Briefly press any button on this device’s remote, close to the box.
SETUP_TIMEOUT_DESC: Check its battery or move closer to the box, then try again. You can also carry on without it: the default settings suit most motors.
SETUP_REMOTE_OK_DESC: The protocol has been set from it.
SETUP_REMOTE_KNOWN_DESC: It can control several devices at once. The protocol has still been taken from it.
SETUP_REMOTE_KEEP: Link it to this device, so its presses update the displayed position
SETUP_ADV_NOTE: The default values suit the vast majority of Somfy RTS motors. Only change the ID to reuse the one from a previous box.
SETUP_PAIR_OPEN: Open the motor’s memory: on {remote}, hold the Prog button (often on the back) until the device makes a short back-and-forth.
SETUP_PAIR_ANY_REMOTE: a remote that is already paired
SETUP_PAIR_2MIN: The memory stays open for about 2 minutes: no need to rush.
SETUP_PAIR_PROG: Press PROG: ESPSomfy-RTS introduces itself to the motor, which should move back and forth again.
SETUP_PAIR_HELP: Don’t worry: the memory may have closed, or the press was too short.
SETUP_PAIR_HELP_2: Try PROG again, holding it for a second. If nothing moves still, reopen the memory with the original remote and start again.
SETUP_TW_PAIR_DESC: The motor learns the ESPSomfy-RTS address, like that of a new remote.
SETUP_TW_UNPAIR_DESC: The motor forgets the ESPSomfy-RTS address; other remotes stay paired.
SETUP_TW_S1_DONE_D: The device jogged back and forth.
SETUP_TW_PAIR_OK_D: Pair again if the device stops responding; unpair it before removing or giving it away.
SETUP_TW_HINT_REMOTE: Press a button on the remote, close to the device.
SETUP_TW_DESC_DIR: We check that Up really raises the device; otherwise the direction is reversed.
SETUP_TW_DESC_CAL: To show an accurate position, ESPSomfy-RTS needs the duration of a full travel.
SETUP_TW_DESC_TILT: The time the slats take to tilt fully, in each direction.
SETUP_TW_DESC_ORDER: What moves first when the motor starts: the slats or the device, in each direction.
SETUP_TW_DESC_OPTS: Favorite position, sun sensor, display, radio range and LED.
SETUP_FLIPPED_NOTE: The commands have been reversed. Let’s check it is right now.
SETUP_NO_REACT: The device did not react: the pairing probably did not take.
SETUP_TEST_PRESS: Press the button and watch the device.
SETUP_CAL_INTRO: To show an accurate position, ESPSomfy-RTS needs to know how long a full travel takes. We time it together: you start it, and click when the device reaches its end stop.
SETUP_CAL_INTRO_2: Stand where you can see the device clearly from start to finish.
SETUP_CAL_TILT_AFTER: The slat tilt is measured just after.
SETUP_CAL_SIMPLE: The device must be fully {pos}. Click Start, then “{btn}” as soon as it reaches its end stop.
SETUP_CAL_KNOWN_RUN: I know the times: enter them
SETUP_DZ_Q: Do the slats pack together at the end of closing?
SETUP_DZ_EXPLAIN: On many devices, at the end of {theDown}, the motor keeps going for a few seconds once the bottom has landed: the slats pack together and the gaps between them close. At the start of {theUp}, it is the other way round: the slats spread apart first, then the bottom lifts off. During that time, the displayed position does not move. If the slats stay apart once at the bottom, there is nothing to measure.
SETUP_DZ_WHY: Measuring it lets the device stop at the right height when you ask for a position.
SETUP_DZ_UP_INSTR: We redo {the} in two steps. The device must be fully {pos}. After Start, click once when the slats have finished spreading apart and the bottom lifts off, then a second time when it reaches its end stop.
SETUP_DZ_DOWN_INSTR: Same for {the}. The device must be fully {pos}. After Start, click once when the bottom lands and the slats start packing together, then a second time when the motor stops.
SETUP_NO_DZ: No slat packing in this direction
SETUP_MID_Q: Fine tuning: does its speed change along the way?
SETUP_MID_EXPLAIN: A curtain that winds onto a tube does not move at a constant speed: the roll grows as it winds, so the device moves faster when it is nearly {open}. If a 50 % command does not stop it halfway, time the halfway point in each direction.
SETUP_MID_LATER: Optional: you can come back to it at any time from the device page, Travel time line.
SETUP_MID_CLEAR: Go back to a constant speed
SETUP_MID_INSTR: The device must be fully {pos}. Click Start, then “{btn}” when it has covered half of its travel. It then carries on to its end stop.
DEVICE_DEADZONE_DESC: Time during which the motor runs while the slats pack together (end of closing) or spread apart (start of opening). The position does not move during that time.
DEVICE_MIDCOURSE_DESC: The motor turns at a fixed speed, but the bigger the roll, the faster the device moves. Enter the time it takes to reach the halfway point from an end stop.
SETUP_ERR_TIMES: Travel times must be between 0.5 and 180 seconds.
SETUP_ERR_TILT_TIMES: Slat times must be between 0.5 and 180 seconds.
SETUP_TILT_INTRO: We measure how long the slats take to tilt fully, in each direction.
SETUP_TILT_INTRO_INTEGRATED: Your motor tilts the slats before moving the device: we measure how long this tilt lasts, in each direction.
DEVICE_TILT_FIRST_ON_OPEN_DESC: Disable if the motor opens the device before tilting the slats
DEVICE_TILT_FIRST_ON_CLOSE_DESC: Disable if the motor closes the device before tilting the slats
SETUP_MY_Q: Does your motor have a favourite position set (My button)?
SETUP_MY_DESC: An intermediate position stored in the motor: pressing My while it is stopped sends the device there.
SETUP_ANSWER_REQUIRED: An answer is needed to confirm.
SETUP_MY_CHECK: Let’s check: with the device stopped, press My. If it moves to a position and stops, one is set.
SETUP_NEED_TIMES: For this, ESPSomfy-RTS first needs to know the device’s travel times.
SETUP_MY_TILTONLY: For a tilt-only blind, the favourite slat position is set from its details page.
SETUP_MY_LEARN_INFO: Let’s teach it to ESPSomfy-RTS. Otherwise, when you press My, the motor does go to its favourite position, but ESPSomfy-RTS does not know where it stops: the displayed position becomes wrong.
SETUP_MY_LATER_NOTE: All right. Until it is learned, the displayed position will be wrong after each press of My.
SETUP_MY_STEP1: 1. Bring the device fully {open}: this is where the measurement starts.
SETUP_MY_STEP2: 2. Press My: the device heads for its favourite position. Click as soon as it stops.
SETUP_MY_WHY: Why this timer? The motor stops at its favourite position on its own, without sending anything: so ESPSomfy-RTS cannot know where it stopped. Your click gives it the travel duration, and therefore the position. The time you take to click is subtracted automatically.
SETUP_MY_WARN_NOMOVE: It barely moved: its favourite position may be right at the top, or not set.
SETUP_MY_WARN_END: It went all the way to its end stop: its favourite position may not be set.
SETUP_MY_CALC: Click at {raw}, minus {react} of reaction time: {t} out of {useful} of useful {what}.
SETUP_MY_ON_MOTOR_DESC: It will be stored in the motor: the original remote will be able to use it too.
SETUP_MY_SIMULATE_DESC: ESPSomfy-RTS will bring the device to this position itself when you press My. The original remote will not know it.
SETUP_MY_PROG_NOTE: The device will go there, then a long press of My will store it in the motor, which will confirm with a short back-and-forth.
SETUP_MY_PROG_Q: Once the device reached {pos} %, did it make a short back-and-forth?
SETUP_SUN_Q: Is a sun sensor paired with this motor?
SETUP_SUN_DESC: A small sensor fitted near the device, which controls it according to sunshine.
SETUP_PARTIAL_DESC: Everything done so far is already saved. Some steps remain: its card will remind you, and you can resume them from the device list.
SETUP_LINK_ALREADY: This remote is already linked to this device.
SETUP_LINK_SHARED: It also controls “{name}”: a remote can control several devices.
SETUP_LINK_TIMEOUT_DESC: Check its battery or move closer to the box, then try again.
SETUP_TIP_RESUME: Unfinished steps can be resumed one at a time: click a setup row to redo it without going through the whole wizard again.
SETUP_TIP_DIR: If the device moves the wrong way, no need to pair it again: the “Direction” row reverses it at any time.
SETUP_TIP_REACH: If this device does not always respond, raise its repeat count in the Settings tab of its page.
SETUP_POS_DESC: The device position is shown as a percentage, in the direction you choose.
SETUP_REACH_DESC: Each repeat sends the command again: raise them for a distant device or one behind a thick wall. When unsure, keep “1 time”: you can change it later from its page.
SETUP_REACH_HINT: If unsure, leave it on “Normal”: you can raise it later from its form if a device does not always respond.
SETUP_LED_Q: Blink the status LED on each command?
SETUP_LED_Q_BOX_WIFI: Blink the box's blue LED on each command?
SETUP_LED_Q_BOX_ETH: Blink the box's green LED on each command?
SETUP_MY_TILT_HINT: The stopwatch only measures travel: estimate by eye the slat tilt at the favourite position.
UNPAIR_DEVICE_STEP_1_1: Open the device's memory using an existing remote: press the Prog button (usually on the back) until the device jogs briefly.
UNPAIR_DEVICE_STEP_2_1: Now press the PROG button below to send the unpairing signal to your equipment.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_NONE_DESC: This device does not tilt its slats -- only its travel (open/close) will be measured.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_TILTMOTOR_DESC: A second motor tilts the slats independently of travel. Travel and tilt will be measured separately.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_INTEGRATED_DESC: The same motor tilts the slats then moves the device (or the reverse) -- the wizard will also ask which happens first.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_TILTONLY_DESC: This device has no travel -- only the slat tilt will be measured.
CAL_BLIND_OPT_EUROMODE_DESC: Travel and tilt handled together by the same motor, with no order ambiguity to detect.
CAL_TILT_UP_INSTRUCTION: The slats must be fully closed before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats are flat.
CAL_TILT_UP_INSTRUCTION_INTEGRATED: The slats must be fully closed before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats stop moving and the device starts to travel -- that is the end of the tilt phase.
CAL_TILT_DOWN_INSTRUCTION: The slats must be fully flat before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats are fully closed.
CAL_TILT_DOWN_INSTRUCTION_INTEGRATED: The slats must be fully flat before starting. Click Start, then Stop as soon as the slats stop moving and the device starts to travel -- that is the end of the tilt phase.
CAL_ORDER_INTRO: Some integrated tilt motors tilt the slats before moving the device, others do the opposite depending on direction. Test each direction and watch what happens first.
CAL_ERR_DURATION_TOO_SHORT: Too short for a real movement -- measurement ignored, try again.
CAL_ERR_DURATION_TOO_LONG: Too long (> 180 s) -- measurement ignored, try again.
CAL_ADJUST_INTRO: Measured time doesn't quite match the real movement?
CAL_ADJUST_TOO_EARLY_DESC: The marker was set before the actual event -- adds 0.1 s.
CAL_ADJUST_TOO_LATE_DESC: The marker was set after the actual event -- removes 0.1 s.
REMOTESLIST_SEARCH: Searching… Press any button on the remote to link it.
PAGE_GROUPS_DESC: A group drives several devices in one action, with its own radio address.
EMPTY_GROUP_DESC: Bring several devices together in a group to control them in one go.
GROUP_CREATE_DESC: Save basic parameters to create your group
GROUP_LED_FEEDBACK_DESC: Flash the status LED once per group command
GROUP_ID_DESC: The group has its own address: every paired device has learned it. Changing it means pairing them again.
GROUP_DELETE_DESC: Deleting the group does not delete its devices: they stay controllable one by one. Remove them from the group first.
GROUP_MEMBERS_TIP: Pairing a device with the group teaches it the group's address: it must be in range, and the operation goes through its memory (Prog).
GROUP_LINK_DESC: Choose, then pair step by step
GSETUP_MEMBERS_Q: Which devices should this group control?
GSETUP_MEMBERS_DESC: Each ticked device will be paired with the group in the next step, one at a time. You can add more later.
GSETUP_NO_DEVICE: No device to add: create a device first.
GSETUP_ADV_NOTE: The group has its own radio address, separate from each device's.
GSETUP_W_HINT_LINK: Pair each device, one by one
GSETUP_MEM_DESC: ESPSomfy-RTS sends a long Prog press with this device's address. Its motor should make a short jog: it is then ready to learn the group address.
GSETUP_MEM_DESC_UN: ESPSomfy-RTS sends a long Prog press with this device's address. Its motor should make a short jog: it is then ready to forget the group address.
GSETUP_MEM_NO: The motor did not receive the press. Check that “{name}” is paired and in range, then try again. You can also open its memory with its original remote (long Prog press): in that case, go straight to the next step.
GSETUP_MEM_OTHER: I opened the memory another way
GSETUP_UNGRP_DESC: The group sends a short Prog press with its own address: the motor forgets the group and makes another jog.
GSETUP_GRP_DESC: Hold the button: the group sends Prog with its own address until the motor makes another jog. Release as soon as it moves.
GSETUP_PICK_Q: Which device should be paired with this group?
GSETUP_L_PICK_DESC: Only devices not yet in “{name}” are listed.
GSETUP_L_PAIR_T: Long press on the group’s Prog
GSETUP_L_UNPAIR_T: Short press on the group’s Prog
GSETUP_L_UNDONE: “{name}” no longer responds to the group
GSETUP_FLIP_DESC: Only reverse it if every device in the group goes the wrong way when the group goes up.
GSETUP_REACH_DESC: “Strong” repeats each command 3 times, for a group with a distant device.
GSETUP_LED_Q: Blink the status LED on each group command?
GSETUP_LED_Q_BOX_WIFI: Blink the box's blue LED on each group command?
GSETUP_LED_Q_BOX_ETH: Blink the box's green LED on each group command?
GSETUP_PARTIAL_DESC: Devices not paired with the group are not part of it: pair them later with “Link a Device” on the group's form.
GSETUP_READY_DESC: All devices respond to the group.
PAGE_ROOMS_DESC: Rooms sort devices and groups into sections on the dashboard.
LIST_ROOMS_NOTE: In “My order” mode, drag a room to change its place on the dashboard.
EMPTY_ROOM_DESC: Create rooms to sort your devices and groups by area on the dashboard.
ROOM_TITLE_ADD_DESC: A name is enough. You can put devices and groups in it right away.
ROOM_TITLE_EDIT_DESC: The name is the section title on the dashboard; what the room holds is listed under it.
ROOM_WIN_SECTION_ADD: Name the room and fill it
ROOM_WIN_CONTENT_HINT: Tick to put it here. An item is in one room at a time.
ROOM_WIN_INLINE_INFO: “{NAME}” will join this room as soon as it is created. Its form stays open behind, with its pending changes.
ROOM_WIN_HINT_NAME: Give it a name to continue.
ROOM_WIN_HINT_LATER: You can put devices here later.
ROOM_WIN_HINT_INLINE: Once created, the room is chosen for “{NAME}” right away.
PAGE_SCHEDULES_DESC: Commands this device sends on its own, at a set time or at sunrise and sunset.
LIST_GEO_NOTE: Sun-based schedules need a geographic position.
LIST_SEARCH_SCHEDULES: Search for a device, a time…
LIST_ADD_SCHEDULE_DESC: A time or the sun, an action, days
EMPTY_SCHEDULE_DESC: A schedule sends a command at a set time or at sunrise and sunset, on the days you choose.
SCHEDULE_CREATE_DESC: Set up one or more time-based triggers for a device or a group.
SCHEDULE_EDIT_DESC: Adjust the settings for this schedule.
SCHEDULE_NO_TARGET_MSG: A schedule must control a device or a group. Create one before setting up a schedule.
SCHEDULE_SUN_NOT_CONFIGURED: Geographic position not configured. Set it in Preferences → Position to use sunrise/sunset.
SCHEDULE_MY_GROUP_NOTE: Devices in this group that don't support the My position (e.g. garage doors) will ignore this command.
SCHEDULE_TILT_GROUP_NOTE: Devices in this group that don't have tilt will ignore this command; their height stays unchanged.
SCHEDULE_SUN_NO_EVENT_TODAY: The sun does not rise or set today at this latitude (polar day/night).
SCHEDULE_ENABLED_DESC: When off, the trigger stays in the schedule but never fires.
SCHEDULE_HOUR_SUMMARY_MY: Will move to My position at {time}
RADIO_ASSIST_DESC: Test your remotes one by one: the assistant adjusts listening if needed.
RADIO_SCAN_HINT_DESC: The 433 MHz band signal in real time. It keeps the strongest frequency.
RADIO_BOX_PRESET: Wired and set at the factory: nothing to adjust here.
RADIO_BOARD_DESC: A known board fills in the pins.
RADIO_SAFETY_TEXT: I have checked my wiring, pin by pin.
RADIO_SAFETY_HINT: A wrong pin can lock up the board or damage it.
RADIO_REMOTES_OFF_DESC: Turn it on and save: without it, ESPSomfy-RTS hears no remote.
RADIO_REMOTES_WIZ_DONE_DESC: Run the test again to confirm that all your remotes are recognised with the new settings.
RADIO_FLEET_CTA_DESC: One by one, within range of the device.
RADIO_FLEET_PAUSED_DESC: Remotes tested so far: {n}. You can pick up where you left off.
RADIO_FLEET_SHIFT_DESC: At least one remote transmits outside the current listening window. The assistant proposes settings that cover them all.
RADIO_FLEET_OTHER_DESC: Its frequency is already inside the listening window: check decoding, the battery or the range.
RADIO_TUNER_ALT: Listening window from {min} to {max} MHz, {bande} kHz wide; transmitting at {tx} MHz.
RADIO_OFF_MSG: Enable the radio at the top of this page, then save: without it, ESPSomfy-RTS hears nothing and this test cannot succeed.
RADIO_OFF_UNSAVED: You have enabled the radio but the change has not been saved yet. Click Save, then try again.
RADIO_TX_STD_DESC: Choose your motors' standard. Most motors use RTS.
RADIO_GROUP_TX_DESC: A device responds poorly? Raise the power first.
RADIO_HELP_TX_FREQUENCY: The frequency on which ESPSomfy-RTS commands your motors: 433.42 MHz (RTS) or 433.92 MHz (RTV). A motor does not drift, or very little, over the years.
RADIO_HELP_TX_POWER: The strength of the signal sent to your motors. 10 dBm is enough for a house. If a distant device responds poorly, raise it first, before touching the frequency.
RADIO_GROUP_RX_DESC: Set by the assistant or the scan.
RADIO_HELP_RX_FREQUENCY: The frequency on which ESPSomfy-RTS listens to your remotes. Over the years, a remote can drift slightly. Your motors are not affected.
RADIO_HELP_RX_BANDWIDTH: The margin accepted around that frequency. Wider, it catches drifted remotes but lets more interference through. The default value almost always suits.
RADIO_HELP_RX_DECODE: How the received message is read: protocol and number of bits. A remote that is heard but not recognised often comes down to this.
RADIO_DECODE_DESC: What the radio expects from your remotes.
RADIO_RESET_DESC: Restores the default radio settings, except the pins. Then run the test again.
RADIO_WIZ_STEP1_DESC: Those already recognised need nothing. For the others, the assistant suggests a setting.
RADIO_WIZ_INTRO_A_DESC: Any button. A short press is enough.
RADIO_WIZ_INTRO_B_DESC: The assistant measures its frequency: hold the button then.
RADIO_WIZ_INTRO_C_DESC: Nothing is saved without your consent.
RADIO_WIZ_DUP_TITLE: This remote has already been tested
RADIO_WIZ_DUP_DESC: It is remote {n} (ID {id}). Press a remote you have not tested yet.
RADIO_WIZ_DECODE_DESC: Any button, within range of the device. A short press is enough.
RADIO_WIZ_OK_DESC: ID {id}, received at {rssi} dBm. It works with the current settings.
RADIO_WIZ_NOTREC_DESC: Nothing was decoded with the current settings. Check the battery and range, or measure its frequency: then hold a button down during the measurement.
RADIO_WIZ_PRESS_DESC: Hold a button down, about one metre away. If it stops, release and press again.
RADIO_WIZ_SHIFT_DESC: It transmits on {freq} MHz, outside the listening window ({min} – {max} MHz): the frequency will need adjusting.
RADIO_WIZ_INWIN_DESC: It transmits on {freq} MHz, already inside the listening window: the frequency is not the cause. Check decoding, battery or range.
RADIO_WIZ_SILENT_DESC: Nothing was picked up. Check that you are holding a button down, that the battery is not flat, and that you are about one metre from the device.
RADIO_WIZ_PARTIAL_DESC: A signal was picked up, but too briefly to be measured. Press again and hold the button until the measurement appears.
RADIO_WIZ_END_OK_DESC: No need to change the frequencies: ESPSomfy-RTS hears them with the current settings.
RADIO_WIZ_END_OTHER_DESC: Changing the frequency would not help: the unrecognised remotes already transmit inside the listening window.
RADIO_WIZ_OUTLIER_TITLE: One measurement does not match the others
RADIO_WIZ_OUTLIER_DESC: Remote {n}, at {freq} MHz, is far from the others ({ecart} kHz apart): probably another device. Keeping it would degrade reception for all.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_MIXED: Recognised: {ok}, to adjust: {shift}. These settings cover them all: save them, then run the test again to confirm.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_STOCK: Your remotes are closely grouped: the factory bandwidth suits them. Only the frequency has been aligned to them.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_WIDENED: Your remotes do not all transmit on the same frequency. The bandwidth has been widened just enough to cover them all.
RADIO_WIZ_TX_KEPT: Transmission to your devices stays at {f} MHz.
RADIO_WIZ_RESULT_HINT: Nothing is saved until you confirm.
SCANFREQ_SCAN_DESC: Hold a button on your remote: ESPSomfy-RTS keeps the frequency where it hears it best.
SCANFREQ_HOLD_DESC: Keep the button pressed, about one metre away. If it stops, release and press again.
SCANFREQ_NO_SIGNAL_DESC: Keep the button pressed, move closer and check the battery.
REPEATER_FRAMES: Frames repeated since this page opened
REPEATER_NO_FRAME: No frame since the page opened
REPEATER_LIST_DESC: ESPSomfy-RTS retransmits every frame received from these remotes.
REPEATER_CAPTURE_DESC: Press any button and its signals will be repeated right away
REPEATER_WIN_DESC: Its signals will be re-sent at once, for a motor that hears it poorly.
REPEATER_WIN_WARN: Only if the motor hears poorly a remote that ESPSomfy-RTS hears well. Never the same one on two devices: echo.
REPEATER_LISTEN_DESC: Any button, near the device. It is linked from the first frame.
REPEATER_LINKED_DESC: The signals of this remote are now repeated.
LOG_DESC: View real-time intercepted frames from your remotes for identification or debugging purposes
LOG_SRC_DESC: Each ID heard, listed once. Tap one to see only its frames.
LOG_TIP: The log fills up from the moment the interface opens and is cleared when the page reloads. An “invalid” frame was picked up but badly decoded (weak signal or interference): it is ignored and controls nothing.
LOG_FILTER: Filter by address, command or code…
LOG_EMPTY_DESC: Press a button on a remote within range: every frame received will appear here.
LOG_NOMATCH_DESC: Change or clear the filter to see all captured frames again.
CONNEXION_TIP_AP: If no network can be reached, the device opens its own access point, named after the device, on 192.168.4.1: that is where you reconfigure it.
CONNEXION_AP_NOTE: You are connected to the device's access point. Choose how to link it to your network.
CONNEXION_ETH_FALLBACK_DESC: Switches to Wi-Fi if Ethernet stops responding
CONNEXION_ETH_PRESET_DESC: Filled in from the chosen model: nothing to set.
CONNEXION_NEAR_IDLE: Start a search to see the Wi-Fi networks the device can pick up. It takes a few seconds.
CONNEXION_HIDDEN_SSID_DESC: Allows connection to a network that does not broadcast its name
CONNEXION_ROAMING_DESC: Always targets the nearest Wi-Fi access point
CONNEXION_HOSTNAME_TIP: The hostname gives the device its local address. A change applies to the network right away, but the new .local address only answers after a restart.
CONNEXION_UPNP_DESC: Announces the device on the local network so other systems find it on their own.
CONNEXION_UPNP_NOW: Applied as soon as it changes, without Save.
CONNEXION_IP_TIP: To always keep the same address, reserve it in your router instead.
CONNEXION_AP_PASSWORD_DESC: Choose whether the access point emitted by the device requires a password
AP_MODAL_WARNING: If you forget this password and the main Wi-Fi fails, you will no longer be able to reconfigure the device remotely: you will need to perform a reset by accessing the restoration page via power cycles (3 quick power cuts).
AP_MODAL_OPEN_WARNING: Without a password, this access point is open: anyone within range can connect to it and control your devices for as long as it stays up.
DHCP_OVERLAY_REBOOT_INFO: Settings will only be applied after the device restarts.
ETH_SETTINGS_WARNING_DESC_1: Wrong pins can damage the ESP32
ETH_CONFIRM_CHECK: Compare these values with the manufacturer's documentation.
ETH_CONFIRM_QUESTION: Do these values match your board?
ETH_CONFIRM_HINT: You can still cancel at the next step.
SAVEWIFI_INTRO: The device saves, then switches network: this page will lose the connection.
SAVEWIFI_AFTER_DESC_2: Or the IP address your router gives it.
SAVEWIFI_STEP_1: Go back to your usual Wi-Fi.
SAVEWIFI_STEP_2: Open one of the addresses above.
HA_HERO_DESC: Your device works perfectly on its own. With a Home Assistant server, this optional integration takes it further.
HA_REQ: Home Assistant 2026.11 or later. On an older version, use
HA_BENEFIT_1: All your devices, nothing to type
HA_BENEFIT_1_DESC: Shutters, blinds, gates… appear on their own as standard cover entities, with their position and tilt.
HA_BENEFIT_2_DESC: Tracked in real time, even when the device is driven by a physical remote.
HA_BENEFIT_3_DESC: From the Home Assistant app, your dashboards and your voice assistant.
HA_AUTO_1: the indoor temperature exceeds 26 °C and the sun is on the south façade
HA_AUTO_1_THEN: lower the blinds on that façade to 30 %
HA_AUTO_2: the weather station reports strong gusts of wind
HA_AUTO_2_THEN: tell the device, to raise the blinds
HA_AUTO_3_THEN: open everything to clear the exits
MARKETP_INSTALL_TITLE: How to install it from the Marketplace?
HA_STEP_1: Open the integration in the Marketplace with the blue button, or search for “ESPSomfy-RTS Enhanced” in Settings → Marketplace.
MARKETP_INSTALL_STEP_2: Download the integration, then restart Home Assistant.
HA_STEP_3: Go to Settings → Devices & services: your device is discovered automatically.
HA_ALT_DESC: For a setup that already goes through an MQTT broker.
HA_MQTT_OFF: The MQTT client is off: nothing is published to Home Assistant.
MQTT_PUB_DISCOVERY_DESC: Home Assistant creates the devices by itself, with no manual setup
MQTT_DISCOVERY_TOPIC_DESC: “homeassistant” for Home Assistant, unless you changed it on your side.
MQTT_DISCO_OFF_NOTE: Discovery disabled: nothing is published under this topic.
MQTT_DISCO_RESTART: After a topic change, Home Assistant may need a restart to see the new configs.
MQTT_OFF_NOTE: The client is disabled: these settings are kept but nothing is sent to the broker.
MQTT_BROKER_ADDR_DESC: The IP address or name of the MQTT server, for example the one of Home Assistant.
MQTT_TIP_CLEAR: The link is not encrypted: username and password travel in clear text. Prefer a broker on your local network and a dedicated account.
MQTT_ROOT_TOPIC_DESC: The base path of every message from this device.
MQTT_CLIENT_ID_DESC: Must be unique if several devices share the broker.
LISTENER_PAGE_DESC: A remote sitting in a drawer? Capture it: each of its presses can trigger an automation in your home automation system.
LISTENER_TIP: Listening does not block the frame: if the remote also controls a device, a press will move it.
EMPTY_LISTENER_TITLE: No remote is being listened to
EMPTY_LISTENER_DESC: Capture a remote to send its presses to your home automation system.
LISTENER_LIST_DESC: Every press on one of these remotes is captured and time-stamped. Edit the name directly in the tile.
LISTENER_CAPTURE_DESC: Press any button and the remote is added to the list
LISTENER_ALSO_MOVES: This remote also controls “%s”: a press will move it.
LISTENER_WIN_DESC: Its presses will be sent to your home automation system as triggers.
LISTENER_SCAN_STEP_1: Take the remote, or select the desired channel on a multi-channel remote.
LISTENER_ALREADY: This remote is already listened to as “%s”.
LISTENER_NAME_DESC: This name will identify the remote in your home automation system.
LISTENER_NAME_HINT: Without a name, the address is used.
SECURITY_STATE_NONE: No protection: anyone on the local network can do anything
SECURITY_INACTIVE_DESC: Access to ESPSomfy-RTS is not restricted. Anyone on your local network can access and modify the configuration or control your equipment.
SECURITY_PIN_CODE_DESC: A 4-digit code will be asked every time you open the interface. Quick to type, including on a phone.
SECURITY_PASSWORD_DESC: A username and password will be asked every time you open the interface. Stronger than a PIN code, recommended if the device is reachable beyond your home network.
SECURITY_PIN_STORED: A PIN code is already saved on the device.
SECURITY_PASSWORD_STORED: A password is already saved on the device.
SECURITY_SECURE_CONFIG_DESC: Allows free access to the dashboard (device/group control), but requires authentication to modify settings.
SECURITY_HA_NOTE: Home Assistant uses these same credentials to connect to the device.
GENERAL_DESC: Language and appearance of your device
GENERAL_NTP_DESC: Gives the schedules the exact time. The default value almost always works.
GENERAL_TIMEZONE_DESC: Daylight saving time follows the selected time zone.
GENERAL_GEO_TILE_DESC: Used to compute sunrise/sunset times for schedules
GEO_PRIVACY_NOTE: Coordinates are rounded to 2 decimal places (about 1 km) before being saved — enough for minute-level accuracy, without storing your exact address.
GENERAL_DISPLAY_MODE_DESC: “Automatic” follows the browser's light or dark setting.
GENERAL_COLOR_DESC: Customize the accent color of the interface
GENERAL_FEEDBACK_LOCAL: These settings apply to this browser only.
FEEDBACK_VISUAL_COMMANDS_DESC: Visually confirms button presses (up, down, My, toggle, and virtual remote). Very useful if the radio activity indicator is disabled.
FEEDBACK_VISUAL_UI_DESC: Visual effect when clicking general buttons, cards, and interactive elements across the interface (excluding control buttons).
FEEDBACK_VISUAL_FORMS_DESC: Visual highlighting of input fields, dropdown menus, and options when selected.
FEEDBACK_HAPTIC_TOGGLE_DESC: Vibrates the device briefly upon interaction (touchscreens only).
FEEDBACK_HAPTIC_UNSUPPORTED: Not supported by this device or browser.
LANG_MODAL_TITLE_DESC: Download new languages from GitHub, upload a JSON file, or manage installed languages
LANG_MODAL_SECTION: Languages on the device and online catalog
LANG_MODAL_HINT: The selected language applies after the page reloads.
LANG_MODAL_HINT_BUSY: Do not close this window: the browser is relaying the file to the device.
MSG_LANG_RELAY_UNAVAILABLE: Downloading this language requires your device to have Internet access (e.g. mobile data), in addition to being connected to the device's WiFi network.
MSG_LANG_MANUAL_IMPORT_INFO: Automatic download couldn't reach the Internet from this device. Open this link with a device that has Internet access to get the file, then import it below.
MSG_LANG_PENDING_INFO: This language will be downloaded and applied automatically once the device is connected to your Wi-Fi network with Internet access.
FW_TIP_BACKUP: Before an update or a restore, create a backup: the .backup file holds the device configuration and lets you roll back.
FW_UPDATE_UPTODATE: Your system is up to date
FW_UPDATE_CHECK_FAIL_DESC: This browser cannot reach the online catalog
FW_AUTOCHECK_DESC: Done by this browser each time it connects to the device. Nothing is installed without your consent.
FW_CHANNEL_STABLE_DESC: The installed firmware is a published release. The development build remains available from “Choose another version”, after confirmation.
FW_CHANNEL_DEV_DESC: Built on every code change, without being tested: bugs and loss of stability are possible. To go back to a stable release, pick it in “Choose another version”.
FW_LED_TITLE_DESC: Configure the hardware status LED and its visual feedback
FW_BACKUP_DESC: Downloads a .backup file with the whole configuration of this device.
FW_RESTORE_DESC: Reinstalls all or part of a .backup file: this device's own, or that of an old device this one replaces. Before sending, the window shows what the file contains and what it will replace.
FW_RESTORE_FORMATS: v3 backups and older v2 backups (v2.4.6 and later) are accepted.
FW_DEBUG_LOGS_DESC: Displays detailed information on the serial port and browser console (sent radio frames, network requests, etc.). Enable only for troubleshooting: this slightly slows down the device.
FW_REFRESH_CACHE_DESC: Clear the system cache and force reload
FW_FACTORY_DESC: Erases the configuration to start over like a new device. The network connection and the radio can be kept.
FW_CREDITS_BUG_TOOLTIP_0: Issues are reserved for real firmware bugs.
FW_CREDITS_BUG_TOOLTIP_1: A configuration question, or need some help? Check the documentation.
FW_CREDITS_BUG_TOOLTIP_LINK: Or ask your question in the Discussions
FW_CREDITS_BUG_DESC: Report a bug or a functional error
FW_CREDITS_LICENSE_DESC: Provided without any warranty. You may redistribute and modify it under the terms of the AGPL-3.0.
FW_THANKS_DESC: Thanks to everyone who contributed code, translations, testing or bug reports.
FIRMWARE_MT_CACHE: Remember to clear the cache after installation.
FIRMWARE_MT_SAVE_BACKUP_DESC: A backup file will be downloaded to your browser
GIT_INSTALL_DESC: The device downloads the chosen version and installs it by itself.
GIT_INSTALL_STEP3_DESC: Then language packs are sent again
GIT_INSTALL_HINT: The window cannot be closed during the installation.
GIT_RELEASE_CONFIRM_SUB: Once started, the update cannot be interrupted until it finishes.
GIT_RELEASE_CONFIRM_SUB_REINSTALL: Once started, the reinstall cannot be interrupted until it finishes.
GIT_RELEASE_CONFIRM_SUB_DOWNGRADE: This version is OLDER than the one installed. Your configuration will be read back by an older firmware: download the backup before continuing. Once started, the installation cannot be interrupted until it finishes.
GIT_LANG_RESTORE_FAILED: Language pack %1 unavailable, using default language
FIRMWARE_OTA_TITLE_DESC: Automated installation from available GitHub releases
FIRMWARE_OTA_CHANNEL_NOTE: The Developer channel asks for confirmation: untested build.
FIRMWARE_OTA_RELEASE_BETA: You have selected a pre-released beta version that has not been fully tested or published for general use.
FIRMWARE_OTA_RELEASE_DEV: Untested development build: back up your configuration before installing.
FIRMWARE_DEV_CONFIRM: Developer mode offers the latest development build, built automatically and never tested. It may leave the device unusable and require a USB reflash. You alone are responsible for the outcome.
FIRMWARE_DEV_NONE: No development build is available for this device.
FIRMWARE_OTA_NOTE_UPDATE: Click directly on the link above.
FIRMWARE_MA_FIRMWARE_DESC: Upload the Firmware binary file to update the system.
FIRMWARE_MA_HINT: Once started, the upload can no longer be interrupted.
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_FOR_DEVICE: The file that matches your device
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_TOOLTIP_VERSION: [version]: the version you are installing, for example v3.0.0.
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_TOOLTIP_GREEN: Highlighted in green: identifies your hardware. A file that does not contain this exact part is not intended for this device.
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_TOOLTIP_ANYBOARD: This file is the same for all boards: its name does not include any model.
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_TOOLTIP_KIND_FW: The name must contain _ota_: this is the device program, web interface included. A _filesystem_ file comes from older versions and is no longer accepted.
FIRMWARE_MA_FILE_TOOLTIP_BOX: Your device is one of my custom boxes: only a file with the highlighted label above is suitable. Files without it are intended for generic boards.
FIRMWARE_MA_UPDATE_FROM_GITHUB: If you don't have it locally: download from GitHub
LED_MODAL_DESC: Customize how the status LED behaves for system state tracking and radio activity.
LED_MODAL_BOARD_INFO: Your board is recognised: the LED pin and type are already set.
LED_MODAL_GENERIC_INFO: Many ESP32 boards have a built-in LED: pick your board model below to use it as an indicator. If yours has none, wire an LED (with its resistor) to a free GPIO and enter it manually.
LED_MODAL_ENABLE_DESC: Turns the hardware status LED on.
LED_MODAL_PIN_DESC: GPIO the status LED is wired to. Used for the recovery boot window and, optionally, for radio activity.
LED_MODAL_PIN_WARN_12: GPIO 12 (MTDI) is a strapping pin: on some modules it sets the flash voltage and a held level can prevent a later reboot. Prefer another GPIO if you have the choice.
LED_MODAL_ACTIVE_LOW_DESC: Yes if your LED lights up when the GPIO is driven low.
LED_MODAL_COLOR_ACTIVITY_DESC: Color of the flashes signalling a command or a radio frame. At rest, the LED stays off.
LED_MODAL_COLOR_ORDER_DESC: GRB or RGB, depending on the component.
LED_MODAL_RF_BLINK_DESC: The LED will blink with every transmitted or received signal. Reacts to any RTS remote picked up nearby, including those from neighbors depending on your antenna range.
RESTORE_DESC: Recover your configurations and devices from a backup file.
RESTORE_INTRO: The file is first read in your browser: you will see what it contains before choosing what to restore.
RESTORE_OLD_READ: contents read by the device when sent
RESTORE_ROLLING: Rolling codes never go back: the device keeps the higher of the two.
RESTORE_SCHED_LOST: Missing from the file, so deleted: %s
RESTORE_SCHED_DEP: Follow the devices: a schedule targets its device by number, so it can neither be restored without it nor outlive it.
RESTORE_EMPTIED: Missing from the file: Yes empties the current list (%s).
RESTORE_SYSTEM_SUM: Hostname %s, NTP, appearance, LED indicator, location
RESTORE_ETH_IGNORED: The other board's Ethernet wiring is ignored: it only applies to that board.
RESTORE_RADIO_BOARD: Backup from another board (%s): check the pins in Radio afterwards.
RESTORE_OLD_RADIO: File older than v2.5.0: the radio pins will not be restored correctly, check them in Radio.
RESTORE_NEVER: Wi-Fi name and password, MQTT username and password, the interface PIN or password, language packs. They stay those of this device.
RESTORE_CONFIRM_SUB: Once started, the restore cannot be interrupted before it finishes.
ROLLING_DESC: Each command increases it; motors ignore a code older than the last one received. Only use this to take over another device's code.
FLIP_COMMAND_DESC: Reverses the direction of the commands
DRAG_SORT: In “By room” mode, drag a tile to reorder it or move it to another room.
LIST_NOMATCH_DESC: Clear the search or choose another filter.
NAME: Name
LINK_PRESS_TITLE: Press a button on the remote
SAVEBAR_PENDING_DESC: They are not applied to the device yet.
WIFI_HIDDEN_NET: + My network is not listed (hidden network)
PAIR_X_NOTE: The second jog is the motor’s only feedback: this button records it.
PAIR_X_NOTE_LINK: The second jog is the motor’s only feedback: this button adds it to the group.
PAIR_X_NOTE_UNLINK: The second jog is the motor’s only feedback: this button removes it from the group.
PROMPT_SECURITY_CONFIRM_DESACTIVE: The interface will be freely accessible again on the local network.
PROMPT_SECURITY_PIN_TITLE: Protect the interface with a PIN?
PROMPT_SECURITY_PIN_WARNING: Please keep your PIN code in a safe place and do not forget it. The only way to recover a lost PIN code is to fully reload the initialization firmware, which will erase your entire configuration.
PROMPT_SECURITY_PIN_CONFIRM: I have written the PIN down somewhere safe.
PROMPT_SECURITY_PASSWORD_TITLE: Protect the interface with a password?
PROMPT_SECURITY_PASSWORD_WARNING: Please keep your password in a safe place. A forgotten password can only be reset via the recovery access point.
PROMPT_SECURITY_PASSWORD_CONFIRM: I have written the username and password down somewhere safe.
PROMPT_SECURITY_CLEAR_SECRET_DESC: Any change to the security mode will erase the password or PIN code previously saved on the device.
PROMPT_UNLINK_REPEATER_DESC: The device will stop relaying its frames.
PROMPT_UNLINK_REMOTE_DESC: "{name}" will no longer follow its presses. The motor itself still obeys it.
PROMPT_DELETE_ROOM_WARNING: The devices and groups it contains move to the "Home" room.
PROMPT_DELETE_DEVICE_WARNING: If it is paired with a motor, unpair it first: otherwise its address stays in the motor's memory.
PROMPT_GROUP_ROLLING_CONFIRM: The code will go from {OLD} to {CODE}. If it is lower than the one the motors know, they will ignore the group until the counter passes it or until a new pairing.
PROMPT_DEVICE_ROLLING_CONFIRM: The code will go from {OLD} to {CODE}. If it is lower than the one the motor knows, it will ignore the device until the counter passes it or until a new pairing.
PROMPT_DELETE_TARGET_SCHEDULES: {n} schedule(s) targeting it will also be deleted.
PROMPT_REBOOT_CONFIRM_SUB: Commands and Home Assistant will be unavailable for a few seconds. The interface reconnects on its own.
PROMPT_FACTORY_SUB: This cannot be undone: only a backup can bring things back. Erased:
PROMPT_FACTORY_CONS_DEVICES: devices, groups, rooms, schedules and linked remotes
PROMPT_FACTORY_CONS_SETTINGS: settings, security (PIN, password, API token) and MQTT
PROMPT_FACTORY_CONS_LANGS: downloaded languages: only the built-in language remains
PROMPT_FACTORY_CONS_MOTORS: pairing with the motors: they will not respond until paired again or a backup is restored
PROMPT_FACTORY_CHECK: I understand this erase is permanent
PROMPT_DOC_SUB: The guide opens in a new tab, on the project website. Internet access is required.
PROMPT_RADIO_MANUAL_WARNING: Incorrect GPIO pins can cause your ESP32 to crash or bootloop.
PROMPT_RADIO_RESET_MSG: The radio settings will return to their default values and the scan measurement will be erased. As a reminder, nothing is saved until you click Save.
PROMPT_UNSAVED_MSG: If you leave now, your changes will be lost.
PROMPT_ACTION_IN_PROGRESS_MSG: An action is currently in progress. Are you sure you want to close this window?
PROMPT_FREQ_SCAN_MSG: Closing this window will stop the ongoing frequency scan. Do you want to continue?
PROMPT_LANG_ACTION_MSG: A language pack is currently being downloaded or imported. Closing this window now may interrupt the operation. Do you want to continue?
PROMPT_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS_MSG: The update is being installed and cannot be interrupted. Please wait for it to finish — do not close this window or power off the device.
PROMPT_RESTORE_IN_PROGRESS_MSG: The file is being uploaded and processed by the device. Please wait for it to finish — do not close this window or power off the device.
PROMPT_SCHEDULE_MERGE_CONFIRM: {target} already has a schedule on these days. Both will become a single one, with {n} triggers.
PROMPT_UNLINK_LISTENER_DESC: Its presses will no longer be sent to your home automation system.
GIT_RELEASE_SUCCESS_2: Please wait a few moments and then reload the page.
TOAST_LANG_MSG: Your system is set to {LANG}. Would you like to download and install this language?
TOAST_LANG_DOWNLOADING_RELOAD: Downloading the language pack… the page will reload automatically once it is installed.
TOAST_LANG_MISSING_MSG: Your language ({LANG}) is no longer installed, likely due to a firmware update. Would you like to download it again?
TOAST_LANG_PENDING_APPLIED: The {LANG} language has been downloaded and applied automatically.

WAIT_MSG_LANG_IMPORT: Importing the language file… the page will reload.
